audience: Platform engineering team at Litware. They care about developer productivity, code quality, and maintaining security of their proprietary payments codebase.
objective: Secure approval for a 3-week pilot with 8 developers using Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark for internal AI workloads.
context: Litware's platform engineering team consists of 40 developers working on a proprietary payments codebase that cannot be sent to public AI services. The team already uses GitHub Copilot for open-source work and runs builds on a shared CI farm. They want to evaluate code completion, test generation, and Q&A capabilities over internal design docs using an internal AI solution. The pilot will involve 8 developers over 3 weeks with measurements of time to first PR and review rework.
facts: 40 developers work on a proprietary payments codebase
Codebase cannot be sent to public AI services
Team already uses GitHub Copilot for open-source work
Builds run on a shared CI farm
Measure time to first PR and review rework
Device: Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark (Blackwell RTX GPU, 20 CPU cores, 128 GB installed memory).
On this device, Gemma 4 26B decodes at about 72 tokens per second and Qwen3-Coder 30B at about 86 tokens per second (single stream, Local-AI-Bench, October 2026).
guardrails: Do not claim performance improvements over GitHub Copilot
Do not suggest this is a production deployment
Do not mention any specific cost or pricing information
Do not claim the solution works with public AI services
Use only numbers from the fact sheet; label any estimate as an estimate to validate.
Do not claim local AI replaces Microsoft 365 Copilot or any cloud subscription.
Do not claim air-gapped, certified offline or security certification; say disconnected use is validated in the pilot.
Do not cite TOPS or Copilot+ PC certification.
